s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic gastrointestinal symptoms with malabsorption and dermatological manifestations
salient_findings: Brownish macules on the hands and feet
Hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
key_facts: History of cleft lip and palate repair
Multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
Nodular lymphoid lesions in the duodenum
Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic gastrointestinal symptoms with malabsorption and dermatological manifestations
salient_findings: Brownish macules on the hands and feet
Hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
key_facts: History of cleft lip and palate repair
Multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
Nodular lymphoid lesions in the duodenum
Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

shortlist.label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple polyps throughout the colon and rectum, and dermatological manifestations

shortlist.label: Juvenile polyposis syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

shortlist.label: Celiac disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic gastrointestinal symptoms with malabsorption and dermatological manifestations

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic gastrointestinal symptoms with malabsorption and extraintestinal manifestations

shortlist.label: Abetalipoproteinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Mild hypoproteinemia and hypoalbuminemia, and zinc deficiency

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple polyps throughout the colon and rectum, along with a history of recurrent diarrheal episodes since childhood, supports this diagnosis. The patient's age and the specific characteristics of the polyps (sessile and subpedunculated) also align with juvenile polyposis syndrome.

rejected.label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
rejected.why: While it involves polyps, Peutz-Jeghers syndrome typically presents with distinct mucocutaneous melanin deposits and hamartomatous polyps, which are not the primary findings here.

rejected.label: Celiac disease
rejected.why: Celiac disease can cause diarrhea and malabsorption but does not typically present with the formation of numerous polyps throughout the colon and rectum.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: Crohn's disease can cause similar gastrointestinal symptoms but is more commonly associated with inflammation and ulceration rather than the formation of numerous polyps.

rejected.label: Abetalipoproteinemia
rejected.why: This condition involves severe fat malabsorption and specific laboratory findings (very low cholesterol levels), which are not highlighted in the case description.
